summary: A short note on where to find on-line documentation at SRI-ARC, whose NLS system hosted much of the early network's documents. It describes two files that guide users to documentation through links: a NIC locator file and a separate locator for the ARC system's own documents.

plainLanguage.summary: It is a note saying which two signposts to look at to find the instruction manuals stored on one particular computer.

subtitle: Where to find documentation in the NLS system.

tldr.problem: SRI-ARC's NLS (oN-Line System) hosted much of the ARPANET's documentation, but users had difficulty locating the information they needed among the many available files.
tldr.mechanism: Two structured files were created to guide users to documentation through a system of links and branch references: the NIC LOCATOR file for general network documentation, and the ARCLOCATOR file for SRI-ARC system documentation.
tldr.outcome: The locator files became the primary way ARPANET users discovered and accessed documentation at SRI-ARC.

today: RFC 544 documents an early approach to organizing hyperlinked documentation on a network-accessible system. SRI-ARC's NLS and its document collection were precursors to modern web-based documentation systems.

sections.title: Organizing ARPANET Documentation
sections.content:
SRI-ARC, the Stanford Research Institute's Augmentation Research Center, hosted much of the ARPANET's distributed documentation in its NLS (oN-Line System), an innovative hypertext-like environment that supported linked documents and structured browsing. As the collection grew, users needed help locating the specific documents they sought.

To address this, SRI-ARC created two locator files to serve as navigational guides: the NIC LOCATOR for general network documentation and the ARC LOCATOR for system-specific documentation.
sections.plainLanguage: One computer had lots of instruction manuals stored in it, so two librarians made two maps to help people find what they wanted.

sections.title: The NIC and ARC Locator Files
sections.content:
The NIC LOCATOR file was the primary entry point for users seeking network-wide documentation. It organized functional documents through a system of branches (hierarchical document sections) that could be followed to find information about different topics. A branch labeled "ARC SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION" within the NIC LOCATOR directed users to the ARCLOCATOR file.

The ARCLOCATOR file contained documentation specific to the SRI-ARC system itself, introducing users to the many features available for network use and explaining how to use the various ARC capabilities. Both files were formatted in a way that was accessible to inexperienced NLS users, with instructions on how to use the files themselves included as the first branch (branch .1).
sections.plainLanguage: One file had links pointing to different topics. If you wanted to learn about the SRI-ARC computer system, that file had a link to another file that explained it all.

sections.title: Using the Locator Files
sections.content:
To access the NIC LOCATOR, users would load the file using the NLS command: L[oad] F[ile] [NIC]locator CR. Once loaded, users could display the instructions (in branch .1) by typing P[rint] B[ranch] .1 CA wn CA. These commands and the structured branch system made navigation straightforward for users who were familiar with NLS commands.

Users were invited to send suggestions and improvements for the LOCATOR files to Kirk Kelley or NDM (Dean Meyer) at SRI-ARC. This feedback mechanism helped keep the documentation guides current as the network and its documentation collection evolved.
sections.plainLanguage: You typed commands to load the map file, then you could jump to different sections to find what you were looking for. If you had ideas for making it better, you could send a message to the people who built it.
